stem.text: When the temperature of a particular reaction is increased by $10\,{}^{\circ}\text{C}$ (e.g. from $20\,{}^{\circ}\text{C}$ to $30\,{}^{\circ}\text{C}$) the rate of the reaction approximately doubles.
What is the **most** significant reason for this increase?

A.text: a different mechanism for the reaction

B.text: an increased collision frequency of the reactant molecules

C.text: more collisions have energy greater than the activation energy

D.text: a reduced activation energy for the reaction
